scope: Complete category/path inventory with explicit dispositions. Representative source audits are recorded in the plans; this is not a claim that all 530 file bodies or historical PDFs were read.

categories.recommendation: Use graphics examples to identify timing/buffer questions; implement through the existing Qt QPA/Screen backend and current Screen samples. Do not port the old gf_* renderer.
Use current C++20 ownership and supported dependency APIs; validate required Boost consumers separately. Do not add an old Boost layer for facilities already covered by the standard library.
Keep serial/character-device operations inside a typed native service; validate devctl sizes, short I/O, termios configuration, permissions, cancellation and cleanup.
Verify shared-library ABI, constructor/initialization order and missing-dependency errors. Do not unload registered Nitro classes while any runtime or descriptor can still reference their code.
Use current debugger, slog2, kernel/application tracing and crash diagnostics. Capture symbols and candidate identities; redact app data.
Audit deployment closure, RPATH/search paths, native registration and lifetime. Do not expose arbitrary dlopen paths or unload controls to app JavaScript.
Use owned asynchronous storage with bounded reads/writes, permissions and explicit durability/atomic-replace semantics verified on the selected target filesystem.
Measure actual payload sizes, copies, allocator behavior and target memory pressure. A synthetic allocator result is not an application or presentation benchmark.
Use 64-bit-safe sizes/offsets and correct alignment with RAII. Do not import the archived pointer-to-unsigned-int allocator into AArch64.
Audit the framework locking/OCB model, authorization, bounded request work, cancellation and concurrent close. Validate lengths and report actual transferred bytes.
Measure a bounded real transport workload with error/timeout and copy accounting. Keep raw sockets and blocking network work away from the GUI/JS owner.
Modernize messages, pulses, events, synchronization, threads/TLS, clocks/timers, signals and scheduling against QNX 8. Separate ISR/driver work from app APIs.
Use old UI examples as behavior prompts for focus, events, geometry and accessibility. Keep Fabric/Yoga/Qt Quick; do not revive Photon or replace the renderer.
Use explicit process ownership, readiness, bounded child supervision and safe argv/environment contracts. Do not expose arbitrary privileged process management to JavaScript.
Use a narrow versioned service contract and explicit timeout/unknown-outcome semantics. Do not transplant unreviewed legacy stubs or promise exactly-once business execution.
Design the path namespace and native access policy deliberately; review per-operation authorization and target framework rules.
Exercise clients against real resource-manager behavior, including denied open, malformed devctl, short transfers, disconnect and teardown.
Test multicore ownership and affinity only for a measured need. Evaluate priority inversion/starvation and process-shared synchronization; do not copy scheduling constants.
Start with a bounded understandable service fixture and prove readiness, request/reply, permissions, failure and shutdown before adding concurrency.
